subject: chemistry
title: Dissolving Drift: Hydration Enthalpies
welcome_lead: Use hydration enthalpies to explain solubility of salts.
meta_desc: A-Level chemistry adventure on dissolution and hydration enthalpy.
final_note: You measured the warmth of dissolving ions.

concepts.def: Gas ion to aq ion energy; exothermic.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Steps: ionic solid -> gaseous ions (lattice dissociation +); gaseous ions -> aqueous ions (hydration -).

ΔH_solution = ΔH_diss(lattice) + ΔH_hyd(cation) + ΔH_hyd(anion).

More negative for: smaller ion, higher charge (e.g. Mg^2+ more exothermic than Na+).

Down a group: hydration becomes less exothermic (ions larger, lower charge density).

Soluble when total hydration outweighs lattice dissociation, or when entropy term -TΔS makes ΔG<0.

Group 2 sulphates: solubility decreases down group; both lattice and hydration become smaller but hydration decreases faster.

mcqs.q: What state are the ions in when defining lattice enthalpy of formation?
options: Gaseous ions — lattice enthalpy is the energy change when one mole of solid ionic compound forms from its constituent ions in the GAS phase.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
The ions are in aqueous solution before forming the lattice.

mcqs.q: Why is the hydration enthalpy of a small, highly charged ion very exothermic?
options: The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
Hydration enthalpy only depends on the size of the ion, not its charge.
Hydration enthalpy is the same for all ions because water molecules are identical.
Small/highly charged ions form strong ion-dipole attractions with water molecules, releasing a large amount of energy.

mcqs.q: Why can an endothermic reaction still be spontaneous?
options: Endothermic reactions are never spontaneous because they require energy input.
The ions start as solid elements before being assembled into the lattice.
If the entropy increase (TΔS) is large enough to outweigh the positive ΔH, ΔG can still be negative.
All endothermic reactions are spontaneous at room temperature.
